articles.title: Four book logging apps to keep you reading
articles.summary: If you’re an enthusiastic reader who wants to track all your past, current, and future books, these apps can help.
articles.body: A lot of us are feeling tense these days, to say the least. So when you’re being bombarded by disturbing news flashes or angry videos online, it might be a good idea to turn to an old-fashioned method of escape — like a book. If you’re a dedicated reader, though, it may not be enough to simply read. You might want to track each book you’ve read and make notes of what you thought of it or what it said to you. You might want to recommend it to others (or warn them against it). You might like a way to find other interesting volumes to read. And if your life is crowded with other activities, you might want to set reminders to take time to read. Book logging apps can help. For a long time, the most popular app for readers has been Goodreads. On this well-known site, people log their reading habits, give their opinions on what they’ve read, and hold discussions on their favorite genres. But while Goodreads is still a powerhouse, there are alternatives. Here are four apps that can help you track the books that you’ve read and find new ones. While the first two, Goodreads and The StoryGraph, emphasize reviews and community, Bookly and Bookmory concentrate more on helping you stick to your reading goals using timers, notes, and other options. Goodreads [Image: Goodreads is still going strong as a book logging site, but the homepage can be overwhelmed by ads. Before going on to alternatives, it’s a good idea to see where Goodreads is these days. Originally, it was simply a place where you could log the books you’ve read and let people know what you thought of them as well as find and purchase new books (from Amazon and other sources). Now, there are book groups and discussions, the ability to find out what your friends are reading, and the opportunity to ask questions of your favorite authors. If you are a writer, you can publicize new works (and hopefully sell more books) by giving out free copies, buying advertising, or interacting with your readers, among other strategies. Unfortunately, in more recent years, Goodreads has also become known for “review bombing,” in which a book is flooded with one-star ratings and critical reviews, often for political or other reasons, and sometimes by people who have not actually read the book. This has put a pall on the app — and has generated a lot of conversation, both pro and con. In addition, the look of the site has become extremely busy and confusing, with ads taking up a large chunk of screen real estate. But perhaps that is how Goodreads remains completely free to use. The StoryGraph [Image: The StoryGraph’s homepage has a simple and straightforward look, emphasizing future and current reading lists. Of the three alternative apps listed here, The StoryGraph is the one that is closest to Goodreads. You can even move your existing data — books you’ve read and want to read — over from Goodreads; I tried it, and the process was gratifyingly simple. If you prefer to start from scratch, you can get recommendations by taking a survey that has you do things like choose up to five favorite genres and list the types of books you don’t want. The StoryGraph’s homepage has much of the same information that Goodreads has — but is a lot less busy and, as a result, easier to navigate. It shows what you’re currently reading, what you have said you want to read, recommendations based on what is in your other lists, and what’s popular among other readers on The StoryGraph. Also, as with Goodreads, there are giveaways so authors can attract more readers. You can see your reading stats and set up goals (how many books, pages, or hours read this year). There is a community tab where you can follow other readers and check out their reviews of books. And, as with Goodreads, you can select a book, and you’ll be shown a description and a rating based on community reviews. You can then click to see the reviews themselves. You can also view what other publications an author has available by selecting their name. There are also buddy reads, where you read a book alongside up to 14 other people. And there are challenges; for example, to read a book published between 2010–2020 that fits your reader profile but excludes your most-read genre. And finally, you can also buy books through Bookshop US, Bookshop UK, and Blackwell’s. A StoryGraph Plus version for $4.99 a month or $49.99 a year offers additional stats and priority support. However, the free version will probably suit most people looking for a simpler but still useful substitute for Goodreads. Bookly [Image: Bookly tries to help you focus on your reading with timers, notes, and even ambient sounds. With all the distractions we are faced with every day, it’s sometimes hard to keep your focus long enough to sit and read. If that bothers you, Bookly is trying to help. Bookly is a mobile app whose purpose is not just to register what you read (in fact, the free version only allows you to keep up to 10 books in your records); rather, its main purpose is to encourage you to read by letting you track when you read, how long you read, and what you get out of it. Set a time when you want to be reading, and the app will notify you when that time rolls around. You can then time your reading session, pausing to add a quote, a thought, or a new word you’ve come across. You can even run ambient sounds while you’re reading. Once you finish a reading session, you can take some reflection time and write what you are thinking. Reading also earns you virtual diamonds — one for every five minutes of reading — which you can use to, among other things, unlock “awesome costumes” for “Bloo,” the app’s little mascot icon. The app monetizes itself in various ways, some of which can get somewhat pushy. You can buy diamonds — for example, $2.99 gets you 1,500 diamonds. There is also a Pro version that costs $9.99 a month or $29.99 a year and offers cloud backup, reading reports, and personalized suggestions, among other features. Bookmory (iOS / Android) [Image: Bookmory lets you make notes while you read; you can time how long you’ve read or set a countdown for a specific reading period. While Bookmory does let you log the books you read and the books you want to read, the emphasis here is on how much progress you make in reading that book. As with Bookly, you can register a paper book to mark your progress with pages, an ebook to mark your progress with a percentage, or an audiobook to mark your progress with episodes. You can register whether you have purchased the book or have it on loan. (Unfortunately, there is no choice to categorize a book as a free download from, say, Project Gutenberg.) If you’ve already got book lists in Goodreads or a number of other apps, you can import them. Once you’ve added a new book, you hit the timer, and it starts to count down the time you spend reading. You can set a countdown if you need to remind yourself to stop, and you can make notes (or take a screenshot of a page). You are somewhat limited; for example, you can type in your own notes, but if you want to use text from a camera or photo, you need to either become a premium member or watch an ad. Tabs at the bottom of the screen let you write notes about the book, see what books you have read (they are registered as achievements), or share your ratings with others on the app or on Instagram. Like Bookly, the emphasis here is on personal achievement rather than establishing a community of readers — and that’s fine, if that’s what you’re looking for. The free version lets you register an unlimited number of books and notes, set a reading goal, and do cloud backups. A subscription costs $2.99 a month or $28.99 a year and eliminates ads, does an automatic backup, offers you daily stats, and more.

articles.title: Elon Musk Kicked Estranged Daughter Off Health Insurance Right After Saying ‘I’ll Always Love Her,’ Ex-Wife Claims
articles.summary: Justine Wilson speaks out about Musk in a new documentary, which he has slammed as a “hit piece”
articles.body:
Justine Wilson, Elon Musk's first wife, is speaking out in a new documentary — including about the tech titan's estranged relationship with their daughter Vivian Jenna Wilson

"[The] most openly defiant was Jenna," Justine says in Alex Gibney's Musk

Musk has blasted Gibney and his lawyer has threatened legal action over the film

Justine Wilson , Elon Musk's first wife, is speaking out about the very public rift between the Tesla and SpaceX chief and their daughter Vivian Jenna Wilson , who is transgender.

Justine married Musk in 2000 , divorced him in 2008 and is one of the key subjects interviewed in Alex Gibney's new documentary, Musk , which is now open in select theaters and will be released nationwide on Oct. 16.

Gibney, an Oscar-winning documentarian, has been heavily criticized by Musk ahead of his new film's release, with an attorney for Musk threatening legal action for what they argued were factual distortions.

The roughly four-hour movie is a deep dive into the career and personal life of the world's richest man . In it, Justine, an author and mom of six of Musk's children (one of whom died in infancy), says his difficult relationship with Vivian goes back to when she was young.

"She is extremely strong-willed," Justine says in Musk of the 22-year-old model and activist. "Elon and I had five kids and the one who was most openly defiant was Jenna [Vivian's middle name]."

Justine says in the doc that when Vivian was 6 years old, Elon told her, "In this world there are winners and losers. Do you want to be a winner or do you want to be a loser?"

"The subtext there was, 'If you do not follow me and do what I say, you will be a loser,' " Justine adds.

Musk himself did not participate in Gibney's film and has publicly ridiculed it as a "hit piece." Instead — unusually — Gibney recreated a version of him using his past statements.

He and Vivian have traded very public criticisms of each other in recent years, with Musk attacking Vivian's trans identity.

While discussing his relationship with their daughter, Justine talks in Gibney's doc about the "pain" Vivian felt after Musk posted on X (which he has owned since 2022) that he had lost her to the "woke mind virus."

"Elon was telling her, through telling the world, what that point of view actually was," Justine says. "And Elon never tried to repair things, that's not in his nature."

"If a relationship ruptures, then it ruptures," Justine says of Musk's perspective.

Justine says Musk treated Vivian's transition like the "death of a child."

"I was like, 'We actually went through the actual death of an actual child,' " Justine recalls saying, referring to first son Nevada, who was killed at 10 weeks old by sudden infant death syndrome in 2002. "'And what's really happening here is this is a child growing up.' "

Justine says Musk told her to tell Vivian that "I'll always love her" — then cut off her health insurance the next day, after Vivian came out as trans.

More broadly, Justine reflected on what her ex might have been grappling with with their daughter. "If you do your job right as a parent, you get displaced by their life, which is no longer your life. There's a lot of emotion involved with that," she says.

Vivian, a model and activist who dropped her father's famous last name in 2022 , recently made clear her split with her dad over artificial intelligence during an interview with PEOPLE in September.

"Art is emotion through expression," she said while promoting the fall 2026 campaign for Spanish fashion label Desigual titled "Born to Disobey."

"Since emotion is inherently human, AI takes away any underlying intention," she continued, "and replaces it with plagiarized colors and shapes."

Musk is out in theaters nationwide on Oct. 16.

articles.summary: Resumo de notícias da semana entre os dias 3 a 9 de outubro.
articles.body:
Confira o que foi destaque no g1 Centro-Oeste nesta semana, com as notícias mais acessadas entre os dias 3 e 9 de outubro.

O governador eleito de Minas Gerais, Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) também tem uma trajetória ligada à música. Antes de assumir o comando do estado, ele gravou um álbum com 15 canções, entre elas músicas como “Bombril” e “Opala do Cleitinho”.

A reportagem mostra esse lado da trajetória de Cleitinho, que ficou conhecido na região Centro-Oeste de Minas antes de ganhar projeção estadual e conquistar o governo mineiro.

Cleitinho quer continuar morando na mesma casa onde vive há 10 anos — Foto: TV Globo

Mesmo eleito governador de Minas Gerais, Cleitinho Azevedo afirmou que deseja continuar morando na mesma casa onde vive há dez anos, no interior do estado.

A declaração chamou a atenção dos leitores ao abordar como o político pretende conciliar a nova função pública com a vida pessoal e a ligação com o lugar onde construiu sua trajetória.

Ana Elisa é a deputada mais jovem eleita por MG — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Aos 21 anos, Ana Elisa Santos Silva (PT), de Divinópolis, se tornou a deputada federal mais jovem eleita por Minas Gerais. A eleição marcou a entrada da jovem na política nacional e colocou a representatividade de mulheres jovens nos espaços de poder em evidência.

Na reportagem, Ana Elisa fala sobre o significado de conquistar o mandato e a expectativa de que outras mulheres jovens também ocupem cargos de representação política.

“Não quero ser a primeira, nem a última”, afirmou.

articles.title: Kbrum põe fé no reggae com o álbum  'Raggaleluia', lançado no embalo do feat com Anitta em funk de 'Equilibrium II' | G1
articles.body:
Líder do coletivo Jamaicaxias, Kbrum lança o terceiro álbum solo, 'Raggaleluia', com 14 faixas calcadas na cultura do ragga e do reggae — Foto: Wander Scheeffer / Divulgação

♬ Quando Anitta lançou o álbum “Equilibrium II” em 23 de julho, uma voz chamou atenção na faixa “Sal grosso”, funk turbinado com toques de ragga e dancehall. Era a voz do cantor e compositor Paulo Henrique Brum, nascido no Complexo de Mangueirinha, em Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense (RJ), e conhecido no universo pop como Kbrum.

Líder do coletivo Jamaicaxias, criado há cerca de 10 dez anos para disseminar a cultura do dancehall e do soundsystem na cena periférica fluminense, Kbrum lança o terceiro álbum solo, “Raggaleluia”, no embalo da projeção alcançada com o feat com Anitta. É um álbum no qual o artista põe fé no raggae e no reggae.

Com 14 faixas formatadas sob direção musical de Warmando, com produção de Áfricanoise e Carlo, o álbum “Raggaleluia” chegou ao mundo ontem, sexta-feira, 9 de outubro, com capa que expõe expressiva pintura de Rafael Simba – um retrato de um Cristo alado, envolto em manto com as cores da bandeira jamaicana, empunhando uma espada e uma balança da justiça enquanto imobiliza o algoz demoníaco – e com a missão de difundir o ragga e o reggae como um som de força espiritual apaziguadora. Daí a junção de palavras no título “Raggaleluia”.

“Raggaleluia é uma palavra que eu criei a partir da junção de duas outras, ragga e aleluia, esta última associada ao sagrado. E, realmente, o reggae me salvou. Para mim, o reggae é um milagre. É um milagre mesmo. É um canto gospel, de louvor, regozijo e gratidão”, caracteriza Kbrum, crescido em lar evangélico, mas atualmente convertido às religiões de matriz africana.

Composto com inspiração no movimento de reggae entranhado na cultura da Baixada Fluminense, terra de bandas como Cidade Negra, o repertório do álbum “Raggaleluia” também transita pelo samba no interlúdio “Na cabeça”, pelo rock em “Bye bye bye”, pelo dancehall jamaicano em “Fora da lei” e pelo amapiano em “Manipula”.

Ao longo das 14 faixas, Kbrum interage com Bruno Kroz, Clara Ribeiro, Chediak, Gugs, Ludom, Mascotte e Maui, convidados de “Raggaleluia”, álbum que sucede “Puro suco” (2024) na discografia solo de Kbrum.

articles.title: Michael Douglas Recalls Turning to Drug Smuggling After Being Cut Off From Dad Kirk
articles.summary: Michael Douglas admitted he turned to drug smuggling in his youth after his father, Hollywood legend Kirk Douglas, cut him off.
articles.body:
Michael Douglas admitted he turned to drug smuggling in his youth after his father, Hollywood legend Kirk Douglas, cut him off.

The legendary actor and producer opened up about this period in his life during a Friday appearance on HBO's "Real Time With Bill Maher," where he promoted his new memoir, "One Helluva Ride ."

"You and I share something in common about getting through college together," Douglas quipped, prompting Maher to reply with, "We discovered … that when you buy pot in one place and sell it in a different place, the difference between those two amounts can be very good in living your life."

"Especially between East Coast and West Coast," Douglas added.

As Douglas went on, he explained how his father essentially cut him off at age 21, noting, "Dad wrote me a check for $10,000 and said, 'Great son, you're on your own.'"

Yet, as Douglas put it, he still had "a couple of years of tuition left in school," so he had to find a way to pay his bills.

"One time I said, 'Dad, you remember one Christmas you bought me two beautiful Italian soft leather suitcases? Well, I found out that each one of those suitcases could hold 22 kilos of marijuana,'" he recalled to Maher. "I would go back east to see my mom with the clothes on my back and two suitcases. This was called, 'BD: Before Dogs.'"

However, Douglas clarified later on in the interview that he did work a number of normal jobs. Specifically, after Maher applauded Douglas for not relying on his famous father to pay his bills, the Oscar winner shared that he was the "Mobil Man of the Month" while working for a gas station in Connecticut.

Douglas also pushed back on the nepo baby label, wondering why Hollywood faced criticism when family businesses are common place.

"With this 'nepo baby' thing, doesn't every single business, doesn't a father or a mother want their son or daughter to go into the business?" he said. "They have a sign that says 'so and so and sons,' so why pick on show business?"

articles.title: ‘Without a doubt, my first choice was Trisha’: '96' director C Prem Kumar clarifies casting Jaanu amid reports of Jyotika being approached
articles.summary: Vijay Sethupathi and Trisha Krishnan’s romantic drama '96', which was originally released in 2018, continues to find an audience years after its debut.
articles.body: Vijay Sethupathi and Trisha Krishnan’s romantic drama '96', which was originally released in 2018, continues to find an audience years after its debut. The film has returned to theatres for the third time, prompting renewed conversations about its enduring appeal. In a recent interview, director C Prem Kumar reflected on the response to the film and clarified that Trisha was always his first choice to play Jaanu, despite reports that Jyotika had initially been approached for the role.C Prem Kumar on the enduring love for '96'Speaking to NDTV, Prem Kumar said he continues to be surprised by the affection audiences show the film each time he marks its anniversary on social media.“It is overwhelming. Every year, I put up a poster marking the film's anniversary, whether it is two years, three years or eight years of 96. The response I receive every time is mind-blowing. It's unimaginable for a film to receive so much love, even though it is just a movie. It is beyond my comprehension,” he said.The director also recalled writing '96' during the Chennai floods in December 2015. Reflecting on his approach to storytelling, he said he believes that certain stories find their way to him rather than being deliberately chosen by him.“I strongly believe, and I am not saying this out of humility, that the story chooses me. It is not me who chooses the story. That is how 96 happened, and that is how the film with Fahadh Faasil happened as well,” he said.Prem Kumar further revealed that he has completed a script based on an idea he first had in 2002 and plans to begin shooting for the project next.Trisha was always the first choice for Jaanu in '96'Prem Kumar also addressed reports suggesting that Jyotika was initially approached to play Jaanu in '96'. The filmmaker clarified that Trisha was his preferred choice from the beginning, although scheduling conflicts briefly complicated the casting process.“Without a doubt, my first choice was Trisha,” he said.Explaining how the situation was resolved, Prem Kumar said Trisha was committed to several projects at the time, while he already had Vijay Sethupathi’s dates. This led to pressure from various quarters to consider another actor for the role.“There were some date issues as she was working in several films and since I had Vijay Sethupathi's dates, there was pressure from various sides to consider someone else. Then Trisha's schedule was rearranged, and I was able to get her dates to match Sethu's. Everything eventually fell into place. I never thought I would direct ‘96’ when I was writing it. I simply wanted to write a script and give it to a director who could make the film,” he added.C Prem Kumar visualises actors while writing scriptsThe director also spoke about how he imagines particular actors while developing characters and writing screenplays. According to Prem Kumar, he had Vijay Sethupathi and Trisha in mind while writing '96'.He followed a similar approach while writing 'Meiyazhagan', imagining Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan in certain roles. His comments underline the importance of casting in his creative process, even as he maintains that a story’s journey can take unexpected turns.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Alia Bhatt was signed in just two meetings’: Sohum Shah reveals how the actress came on board 'Tumbbad 2' after after a narration, calls her 'very sharp' and praises her business sense
articles.summary: Alia Bhatt agreed to join 'Tumbbad 2' after just two meetings with the film’s team, actor-producer Sohum Shah has revealed.
articles.body: Alia Bhatt agreed to join 'Tumbbad 2' after just two meetings with the film’s team, actor-producer Sohum Shah has revealed. Speaking about the casting process, Shah said the actress responded positively to the screenplay after hearing the narration and reading the script. He also praised her professionalism, sharp understanding of a project’s potential and ability to recognise the strengths of a story.The sequel follows the 2018 fantasy horror film 'Tumbbad', which is set to complete eight years on October 12, 2026.Sohum Shah on Alia Bhatt joining 'Tumbbad 2'In an interview with Variety India, Sohum Shah recalled that Alia was quick to express interest in the sequel after the team narrated the story to her. According to the actor-producer, she subsequently read the screenplay and agreed to come on board, making the process unusually straightforward.“We narrated the script to her and she read it. She immediately said yes. She really liked the script, so it was a very easy process. She is very sincere and professional. The entire process was very smooth,” he said.Alia Bhatt signed 'Tumbbad 2' after two meetingsShah also spoke about Alia’s approach to evaluating the project, recalling that she asked pertinent questions during their first meeting before reading the script over the next few days. When they met again, the casting decision was finalised.“She is very sharp. As good an artiste as she is, I think her business sense is equally good. When we went to meet her, she asked some very pertinent questions. I don’t remember exactly what she asked, but she heard the narration, read the script within two or three days and we met again. Alia Bhatt was signed in just two meetings!” Shah said.The actor-producer added that such a quick decision was uncommon in his experience. He credited Alia’s ability to assess the screenplay and understand its strengths for the smooth casting process.“That doesn’t happen very often. It’s very tough. But she understood the merit of the script, what was there in it and what wasn’t. So, yes, she is very sharp,” he added.Shah also revealed that Alia was already familiar with 'Tumbbad' and liked the original film. He said they shared a similar understanding of the movie, which is often discussed primarily in the context of its horror elements.Sohum Shah says Alia Bhatt's character is significant in 'Tumbbad 2'While the makers have not revealed details about Alia’s character, Shah indicated that her role would make a substantial contribution to the sequel. He expressed confidence in the casting and suggested that audiences would understand the decision once they watch the film.“Alia is in the film, but her character contributes a lot to it. It is very correct casting. When people watch the film, they will understand why it is such a good casting choice,” he said.The makers have yet to disclose further details about the character or how it fits into the story. Alia’s casting nevertheless marks a notable addition to the next chapter of the franchise, which returns to the dark fantasy world established in the original film.'Tumbbad 2' release date, director and castDirected by Adesh Prasad, 'Tumbbad 2' is scheduled to release in theatres on December 3, 2027. Sohum Shah returns as Vinayak Rao, with Alia Bhatt, Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Diorr Varghese also part of the cast. The sequel began production with a mahurat ceremony in Mumbai on April 7, 2026. Its tagline, “Pralay Aayega”, translates to “The apocalypse will come”.While the makers have kept the plot under wraps, the sequel is expected to revisit the unsettling fantasy world that made 'Tumbbad' distinctive.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' continues its theatrical run on Day 9 (second Saturday) after crossing the Rs.
articles.body: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' continues its theatrical run on Day 9 (second Saturday) after crossing the Rs. 400 crore mark in worldwide gross collections on Day 8. The film has stepped into its second weekend with strong numbers. After a Rs. 245.50 crore India net in week 1, Ajay Devgn's thriller added Rs. 14.50 crore on Day 8, which took its India net to Rs. 260 crore and the India gross to Rs. 312 crore. The film has two clear benchmarks ahead. With Day 9 live collections underway, the film has now set its sights on the Rs. 300 crore domestic milestone and a worldwide gross of Rs. 415–420 crore.'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion' domestic box office runThe film opened with Rs. 62 crore net, added Rs. 53.50 crore on Day 2 and jumped to Rs. 61 crore on Day 3. After the first weekday dip to Rs. 21 crore on Day 4, it earned Rs. 19.50 crore on Day 5, Rs. 15.50 crore on Day 6 and Rs. 13 crore on Day 7. That brought the week 1 India net to Rs. 245.50 crore and the India gross to Rs. 294.60 crore. Day 8 saw a small rise, with Rs. 14.50 crore net, taking the total to Rs. 260 crore net and Rs. 312 crore gross.‘Drishyam 3 The Conclusion’ overseas collection and worldwide totalOverseas, the film made Rs. 18.50 crore on Day 1 and Rs. 23.00 crore on Day 2 and Rs. 21.00 crore on Day 3. Day 4 brought Rs. 9.50 crore, followed by Rs. 8.50 crore on Day 5, Rs. 4.50 crore on Day 6 and Rs. 4 crore on Day 7. The overseas gross stood at Rs. 89 crore by the end of week 1, with a worldwide gross of Rs. 383.60 crore. Day 8 added Rs. 6 crore, lifting the overseas total to Rs. 95 crore and the worldwide gross to Rs. 407 crore.'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion' Day 9 collection live trackingAccording to Sacnilk, the film has earned Rs. 13.30 crore net on Day 9 so far through 9,875 shows, and the figure will grow as the day's shows complete.This takes the India net to Rs. 273.30 crore and the India gross to Rs. 327.69 crore. Final Day 9 numbers, along with overseas figures, are yet to be reported.Day wise collections for 'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion'Week 1: Rs. 245.50 croreDay 8: Rs. 14.50 croreDay 9 [LIVE]: Rs. 13.30 croreTOTAL: Rs. 273.30 croreMore about 'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion''Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' serves as the final chapter of the hit Hindi crime-thriller franchise directed by Abhishek Pathak.The film brings Vijay Salgaonkar's story to its final chapter, following 'Drishyam' (2015) and 'Drishyam 2' (2022). Ajay Devgn plays Vijay, a cable operator and movie buff who uses his knowledge of films and human behaviour to shield his family from the law after an accidental death.The core ensemble returns alongside powerful new additions with Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, Tabu as Meera Deshmukh, Shriya Saran as Nandini Salgaonkar, Jaideep Ahlawat as SP Rajveer Singh Tomar, Ishita Dutta as Anju Salgaonkar, Mrunal Jadhav as Anu Salgaonkar, Rajat Kapoor as Mahesh Deshmukh and Prakash Raj as Public Prosecutor Indrajith Shetty.The film was cleared by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) with a UA 16+ rating without cuts, running for a precise duration of 150 minutes (2 hours and 30 minutes).DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and data in this article are compiled from diverse public and industry sources. articles.title: Lance Bass Says He Earned Just $35 a Day at the Height of *NSYNC’s Fame
articles.summary: The singer claimed the group’s first check was $10,000 — after “years of number one albums” and sold-out tours.
articles.body:
Lance Bass has detailed just how little he says he earned during *NSYNC 's rise, claiming he was paid a per diem of $35 a day while the group was one of the biggest acts in the world.

Speaking on The Zach Sang Show , the 47-year-old singer said the money didn't match the band's success. "We had a per diem: $35 a day," Bass said. "Our first check was a $10,000 check after years of No. 1 albums, sellout tours. I don't know how many millions I made off of merchandise, because merchandise was insane." He recalled being told to be grateful for the $10,000: "You should be grateful for that. You've been working for free for two, three years now."

Bass — who rose to fame alongside Justin Timberlake , JC Chasez , Chris Kirkpatrick and Joey Fatone — pushed back on the perception that the group made him wealthy. "People think I'm so filthy rich from *NSYNC, but no," he said. "Not at all. I didn't make money with *NSYNC, like, hardly at all." He said he still receives residuals, but "it's not much," and that he earned far more after the band went on hiatus in 2002.

He alleged that the bulk of the money went elsewhere, claiming "the label" and the group's late manager, Lou Pearlman, "made a f–k ton." Pearlman, the impresario behind *NSYNC and the Backstreet Boys , was convicted in 2008 of money laundering, conspiracy and bankruptcy fraud in connection with a long-running Ponzi scheme; he died in prison in 2016.

Asked whether he still carried resentment, Bass said "not anymore," though he maintained he had been shortchanged. "No one set us up for life after that," he said.

The claims stand in stark contrast to *NSYNC's commercial record. The group remains one of the best-selling acts in Billboard history: their 2000 album No Strings Attached sold a then-record 2.4 million copies in its first week — a mark that stood for 15 years — and spent eight weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 . Its lead single "Bye Bye Bye" became a signature hit, and the follow-up "It's Gonna Be Me" gave the group its only Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 that summer. Their 2001 album Celebrity also debuted at No. 1, while the No Strings Attached tour grossed more than $70 million. *NSYNC reunited briefly for a new single, "Better Place," in 2023.

It isn't the first time Bass has spoken about the band's finances. "We were famous, but we were not rich," he said during a 2023 appearance on SiriusXM's The Jess Cagle Show .

articles.title: Amitabh Bachchan must appear in person if settlement with defendants remains incomplete in personality rights case and to pursue remaining claims, directs Delhi High Court, grants time until November 16
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed Amitabh Bachchan to appear personally at the next hearing if the settlement in his personality rights case remains
articles.body: The Delhi High Court has directed Amitabh Bachchan to appear personally at the next hearing if the settlement in his personality rights case remains incomplete and he wishes to pursue his claims. The court has granted the veteran actor additional time to complete the formalities of a settlement reached with some defendants through mediation. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav has listed the matter for November 16, 2026, while making it clear that Bachchan’s personal appearance will be required if the settlement does not materialise and he wants to continue with the suit.Why the Delhi High Court directed Amitabh Bachchan to appear in personAccording to ANI, the court passed the direction on October 9 after being informed that an amicable settlement had been reached with some defendants. However, the agreement could not be formally signed because of logistical issues on Bachchan’s side. His counsel, advocate Dhruv Anand, sought additional time to complete the formalities and place the settlement agreement on record. The court granted the request and scheduled the next hearing for November 16.The court clarified that if the settlement remains incomplete or fails to materialise, Bachchan must be personally present if he wishes to pursue any of the claims or issues in the suit. The direction does not mean the entire case has been settled or dismissed; the proceedings remain pending.What the court order saysThe court’s order specifies the conditions under which Bachchan must appear at the next hearing. It states:“Time stands granted. List on 16.11.2026. In the event of non-settlement or incomplete settlement, if the plaintiff wishes to pursue the suit on any of the claims or issues, the plaintiff shall remain personally present on the next date of hearing, enabling the Court to exercise its powers under Order X Rule 2 read with Order V Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.”These provisions relate to the court’s powers concerning the examination and personal appearance of parties. The direction is conditional: if the settlement is completed, the situation may differ; if it is not, Bachchan must appear personally to pursue the unresolved claims.Background of Amitabh Bachchan’s personality rights caseBachchan approached the Delhi High Court in 2022 seeking a permanent injunction to protect his personality and publicity rights. On November 25, 2022, the court granted an ex parte ad-interim injunction in his favour, restraining unauthorised use of his personality attributes.The suit alleged that various individuals and entities were exploiting his name, image, voice and celebrity status without permission for commercial gain. The alleged misuse included the unauthorised association of his identity with lottery schemes and other activities, as well as the use of his persona by businesses and merchandise sellers. The actor sought legal protection against such exploitation.Allegations of unauthorised use of his name, image and voiceThe case centres on Bachchan’s request to prevent third parties from using identifiable elements of his persona without his consent. His claims cover his name, likeness, voice and image, which he alleges have been used to promote goods, services and other commercial activities.The interim order granted in November 2022 provided him with protection while the suit proceeded. The subsequent mediation efforts have led to a settlement with some defendants, according to the latest court proceedings. However, the formal agreement still needs to be signed and placed on record, and the case remains pending in relation to any unresolved claims.Lawyers representing Amitabh Bachchan and the defendantsAdvocates Dhruv Anand, Dhananjay Khanna and Bhavya Verma appeared for Bachchan. Advocates Vinay Mohan Sharma, Tina Garg, M. K. Ghosh, Kushal Kumar and Rishabh Saxena represented certain defendants in the proceedings. The matter is scheduled to return to the Delhi High Court on November 16, 2026, when the status of the settlement and any remaining claims will be taken up.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Vijay Deverakonda wins interim personality rights protection from Delhi High Court as platforms directed to content misusing actor's identity within 72 hours, extends protection to AI-generated images and deepfakes
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has granted interim protection to actor Vijay Deverakonda against the unauthorised use of his name, image, voice and other
articles.body: The Delhi High Court has granted interim protection to actor Vijay Deverakonda against the unauthorised use of his name, image, voice and other personality attributes, including through artificial intelligence (AI), deepfakes and face-morphing technology. Justice Vikas Mahajan directed social media platforms to remove identified content allegedly misusing the actor’s identity. The court has also set a 72-hour deadline for specified online marketplaces and domain name registrars to act on identified infringing links and domains.Delhi High Court protects Vijay Deverakonda’s personality rightsAccording to ANI and LiveLaw reports, the Delhi High Court has restrained the unauthorised exploitation of Vijay Deverakonda’s personality attributes. The order directs Meta, Google and X to remove, disable access to and permanently take down identified content, including videos, reels, posts, accounts and channels that allegedly misuse or imitate the actor’s identity.The court directed online marketplaces to remove the specified infringing links within 72 hours of receiving a copy of the order. Domain name registrars were also instructed to lock and suspend the identified domains within the same period.Additionally, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Department of Telecommunications were directed to issue the necessary instructions to internet and telecom service providers to block or remove access to the listed websites within 72 hours. The concerned entities must file compliance affidavits within two weeks, as specified in the order.Order covers AI-generated images, videos and deepfakesVijay Deverakonda approached the court alleging the unauthorised commercial use of his name, photographs, voice and other distinctive attributes. His plea also raised concerns about AI-generated and digitally morphed videos depicting him in obscene, vulgar and objectionable situations. The interim protection covers variations of his name, including “Vijay Deverakonda”, “Vijay Devarakonda” and “Vijay Sai Deverakonda”, as well as his initials, “VD”. It also extends to his voice recordings, signatures, fashion style, photographs, movie stills and performances.The court observed that the actor had established a strong prima facie case for protection. It further noted that the potential damage to his image and personality appeared real and might not be adequately compensated through monetary damages alone. The order seeks to prevent the unauthorised exploitation of the actor’s identity, including for commercial gain and through digitally manipulated material that could harm his reputation.Delhi High Court clarifies protection over ‘Rowdy’While granting interim protection over the actor’s personality attributes, the court declined to issue an ex-parte interim injunction against the standalone use of the word “Rowdy” on the ground of passing off.The court observed that evidence would be required to establish that the term had acquired distinctiveness or a secondary meaning exclusively associated with Deverakonda. However, it clarified that using an AI-generated or morphed image of the actor alongside the word “Rowdy” would fall within the scope of the protection granted for his personality rights.The distinction means that the standalone use of the word has not been prohibited under the interim order, while its use in combination with manipulated images of the actor may amount to a violation of his protected personality attributes.Vijay Deverakonda’s personality rights case: What happens next?The Delhi High Court has issued notice to the defendants and directed them to file their replies within four weeks. The matter is scheduled to come before the Joint Registrar on December 3, 2026, for completion of service and pleadings, followed by a hearing before the court on February 2, 2027.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Nana Patekar was to be our last guest’: Shekhar Suman cancels ‘Shekhar Tonite’ finale says no one can take the late actor’s place, recalls actor’s last phone call and unreleased film ‘Tadap’
articles.summary: Shekhar Suman has decided not to go ahead with the planned finale of ‘Shekhar Tonite’ after the death of Nana Patekar, who was scheduled to be the
articles.body: Shekhar Suman has decided not to go ahead with the planned finale of ‘Shekhar Tonite’ after the death of Nana Patekar, who was scheduled to be the season’s final guest. In a video shared on his YouTube channel, the actor-host remembered his association with the late actor, recalled a phone call in which Patekar praised his show and spoke about their unreleased film, ‘Tadap’. Suman said he did not want to invite anyone else to fill the spot, describing Patekar as irreplaceable.Shekhar Suman says Nana Patekar was to be the final guest on ‘Shekhar Tonite’In the video, Suman revealed that the episode featuring Patekar had been planned as the season finale. Remembering the veteran actor’s qualities, he described him as an artist whose honesty and simplicity stood out.“Words are less to praise the artiste, actor, who was going to appear in this episode. Fearless, brave, honest, a person whose simplicity was his strongest trait,” Suman said.The actor-host explained that he could not bring himself to invite another guest after Patekar’s death. Rather than replace him, he decided to end the first season by remembering the actor and the conversation they had hoped to share with viewers.Shekhar Suman recalls Nana Patekar’s last phone callSuman also recalled speaking to Patekar just days before his death. According to the actor-host, Patekar had called to congratulate him on ‘Shekhar Tonite’ and revealed that he regularly watched the show.“He congratulated me and said that he watches my show regularly. He also told me that he sees himself in me,” Suman recalled.Patekar had also expressed his desire to appear on the show, despite receiving invitations from other programmes.“He said, ‘I get offers from a lot of shows, I don’t go anywhere, but I want to come on your show.’ It felt like I got a Padma Vibhushan,” Suman said, describing how much the actor’s words meant to him.The planned appearance had therefore held special significance for Suman, who was looking forward to a conversation with an actor he deeply admired.Shekhar Suman remembers unreleased film ‘Tadap’ with Nana PatekarSuman reflected on his professional and personal association with Patekar, recalling that they had worked together in Sohanlal Kanwar’s 1990 film ‘Tadap’. Although the film was completed, it never reached theatres.“During that time, I got to know him personally. I learnt a lot from him as a person, and as an actor. Sadly, the film was completed but couldn’t be released. Look at the coincidence, that this episode that was supposed to be shot with him also won’t reach the audience ever. My heart will be upset about this all my life. It would have been the most beautiful conversation with him,” the actor-host said.Drawing a parallel between the unreleased film and the episode that will now remain unaired, Suman expressed regret that audiences would not get to see the two share their conversation on screen.‘He is irreplaceable’: Shekhar Suman on ending the season with Nana Patekar’s memoriesExplaining why he would not bring another guest on the show, Suman said that no one could occupy the place intended for Patekar.“Nana took a permanent break from us. We love you Nana and we will miss you forever. I didn’t feel like inviting anyone else today because no one can take his place. He is irreplaceable. He lived life on his own terms. I had even decided on my opening lines for the episode. I want to end our first season with his memories,” he said.Suman’s decision means that the planned finale featuring Patekar will not go ahead. Instead, the actor-host intends to bring the season to a close by remembering the veteran actor and the conversation they had hoped to share.Nana Patekar dies at 75Nana Patekar reportedly died on October 8 at the age of 75 following a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. His demise prompted tributes from colleagues and members of the film industry, with many remembering his performances, distinctive screen presence and contribution to Indian cinema.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘I have never really felt like a big superstar’: Rajinikanth says he still misses his five years as a Bengaluru bus conductor while promoting ‘Jailer 2’
articles.summary: Rajinikanth has reflected on his life before stardom, revealing that he still misses his days as a bus conductor in Bengaluru.
articles.body: Rajinikanth has reflected on his life before stardom, revealing that he still misses his days as a bus conductor in Bengaluru. During a promotional event for his upcoming film ‘Jailer 2’, the veteran actor spoke about the five years he spent in the profession before entering the film industry. Despite becoming one of Indian cinema’s biggest stars, Rajinikanth said he has never stopped feeling connected to his former job.Rajinikanth says he still misses his bus conductor daysSpeaking at the event, Rajinikanth said that while he enjoys acting, his attachment to his former profession remains strong. He recalled spending five years working as a bus conductor and admitted that he continues to miss those days.“I enjoy acting, but I am also deeply interested in working as a bus conductor. I spent five years working as a bus conductor, and even now, I still miss that job. Deep in my heart, I have always felt a strong connection to the conductor’s job. To be honest, I have never really felt like a big superstar,” he said.The actor’s remarks offered a glimpse into the life he led before achieving fame and reflected the lasting place his early experiences hold in his life.Bengaluru brings back Rajinikanth’s old memoriesRajinikanth also spoke about how visiting Bengaluru takes him back to his years as a bus conductor. He said that seeing buses in the city often brings back memories of that phase of his life.“Whenever I visit the city, I often find myself thinking about my days as a bus conductor. Whenever I see a bus, I feel very happy. Recently, when I visited Bengaluru, I realized once again how deeply connected I am to the job,” he said.He added that his former profession would always remain part of his identity, regardless of his achievements in cinema.“No matter what I do, a part of me will always identify as a bus conductor. Bus conductors will always remain humble in front of big personalities,” the actor said.About ‘Jailer 2’Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, ‘Jailer 2’ features Rajinikanth alongside SJ Suryah, Vidya Balan, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu and Mirnaa. articles.title: Jorge Javier Vázquez y Juls Janeiro, 'unidos' en televisión: "El enano dictador y la nepo baby roja"
articles.standfirst: El presentador confiesa que tiene muchas ganas de conocer a la hija de Jesulín de Ubrique y María José Campanario.
articles.summary: El presentador confiesa que tiene muchas ganas de conocer a la hija de Jesulín de Ubrique y María José Campanario.
articles.body: Jorge Javier Vázquez ha protagonizado un divertido intercambio con Juls Janeiro en el que ha dejado claro que le encantaría conocerla en persona. El presentador, que no ha ocultado su interés por la hija de Jesulín de Ubrique y María José Campanario, ha aprovechado la conversación para plantearle una posibilidad inesperada: que algún día se anime a visitar España y coincidan en un plató de televisión. “Tenía muchas ganas de hablar contigo, me has alegrado el verano”, le ha confesado el comunicador al comienzo de la conversación. Una declaración a la que Juls ha respondido mostrando también sus ganas de conocerlo. El intercambio ha ido ganando complicidad hasta que Jorge Javier ha comenzado a especular con un posible encuentro en Mediaset. Además, aseguró sentirse muy próximo a su interlocutora porque cree que ambos comparten las mismas ideas políticas. Jorge Javier Vázquez: “Me siento muy próximo a ti porque creo que votamos lo mismo”, a lo que Juls Janeiro comentó antes de lanzar una frase en tono distendido en la que hizo referencia a “el enano dictador y la nepo baby roja”, una expresión con la que añadió un toque de ironía a la conversación. Durante la charla, el presentador le ha preguntado si le gustaría viajar a España y acudir a las instalaciones de Mediaset junto a su padre. Juls no ha confirmado que tenga previsto hacerlo, aunque tampoco ha cerrado completamente esa posibilidad. “Yo no cierro las puertas a nada”, ha asegurado Jorge Javier, animándola a mantener la mente abierta ante nuevas experiencias. El comunicador ha insistido en que un encuentro entre ambos podría dar mucho juego televisivo. “Imagínate el dúo que haríamos, ¿qué te parecería? Tú sabes que yo aquí te acojo con los brazos abiertos”, le ha dicho, dejando patente su disposición a compartir espacio con ella ante las cámaras. Además, Jorge Javier ha bromeado sobre la afinidad que cree tener con Juls y ha deslizado que ambos podrían compartir determinadas ideas. La conversación ha mantenido un tono desenfadado, con comentarios espontáneos y referencias a un hipotético encuentro fuera de las pantallas. Por el momento, no hay confirmación de que Juls Janeiro vaya a participar en un programa de Mediaset junto al presentador. Sin embargo, el intercambio ha dejado abierta la puerta a una posible reunión que Jorge Javier parece esperar con entusiasmo.

articles.summary: Michael Douglas alleges a confrontation with Julia Roberts, secret affairs and a cocaine-fueled evening with O.J. Simpson in his new memoir.
articles.body: Michael Douglas is pulling back the curtain on the most explosive moments of his life, both in front of the camera and behind the scenes. In his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," the actor-producer also opens up about secret affairs, heavy cocaine and alcohol use, a "rehab or divorce" ultimatum from his first wife, Diandra, and the painful family struggles that followed him from childhood into fatherhood. "We took Debra to dinner and, once again, it was an epic meal. Any time you have dinner with Jack or Danny, it’s a riot. … But the real goal of the dinner was to get Debra on board to make Romancing the Stone, and no matter how hard we tried, she would not give us an answer, one way or the other. We were stuck in limbo." MICHAEL DOUGLAS ADMITS HE ALMOST LEFT HIS WIFE FOR HIS 'BASIC INSTINCT' CO-STAR AFTER AFFAIR "Stories had filtered back that Debra was delivering an incredible performance in Terms of Endearment, but also that she was difficult during shooting and had huge, blow-out fights with Shirley MacLaine," he wrote. "We all left the restaurant and were walking down the street when, the way somebody might punch you in the arm as you part company, Debra leaned over and bit me. I mean, she really bit me. Jesus, I had a whole set of teeth marks dug into my arm. We still had no answer from her, but that bite sealed the deal for me. No, thank you!" MICHAEL DOUGLAS REVEALS HE MADE FIVE PHONE CALLS TO FIVE WOMEN THE DAY HE CHOSE CATHERINE ZETA-JONES Douglas said he later reenacted the moment for Fox executives, telling them, "She bit me. Hard. Winger ultimately did not join the project, and Kathleen Turner was cast in the role. Fox News Digital has reached out to reps for Winger for comment. Douglas confronted Julia Roberts over his teenage son Douglas experienced another tense moment involving Julia Roberts at a Golden Globes party. Douglas was at the event with his son Cameron, who was about 13 at the time. In the book, Douglas alleges that Roberts had her arm around Cameron and was "kind of nuzzling him." Douglas, who admits he was drunk, claims Cameron looked stunned. BRAD PITT SAYS HE CAN DRINK IN ‘RESTRAINED MANNER’ AFTER 7 SOBER YEARS, BUT EXPERT RAISES RED FLAG "I told her, ‘Take your hands off my son and take that Golden Globe and stick it where the sun don’t shine,’" he writes. Douglas later apologized to Roberts and her then-boyfriend, Kiefer Sutherland. BRAD PITT ADMITS HE BEGAN DRINKING AGAIN AFTER YEARS OF SOBRIETY "I sent Julia roses with an apology for my behavior, and then back in the production office, I apologized to her and Kiefer in person," he wrote. Fox News Digital has reached out to reps for Roberts for comment. Douglas reveals secret affair with Lee Purcell While filming "Adam at 6 A.M." early in his career, Douglas says he and his married co-star Lee Purcell became lovers. "As filming progressed, my relationship with Lee changed and we became lovers," he writes. "Our intimate relationship was complicated by the fact that she was married, and we had to keep it a secret from the cast, crew, the people in the town we were filming in, and of course her husband. It was a passionate affair that lasted through filming." He says he and his first wife, Diandra, were both involved in extramarital relationships as their marriage deteriorated. Fox News Digital has reached out to reps for Purcell for comment. Diandra gave him a ‘rehab or divorce’ ultimatum In the midst of his substance abuse and infidelity, Douglas said his first marriage to Diandra Luker eventually came to a head at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel. After Diandra initially declined to stay with him at the hotel, Douglas called a woman he had been seeing. The woman came to his room, where they had drinks. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "The indiscretion, the drugs, the booze. I was in a constant state of temporary pleasure or temporary escape," he writes. "In my heart, I knew that I was heading down a very bad road at a very high speed, but I was trying my best to compartmentalize…" Douglas entered the Sierra Tucson rehabilitation clinic in Arizona in 1992 to receive treatment for alcohol and substance abuse. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Douglas denies being a sex addict Douglas says his rehab stay was later exploited by a tabloid. He says they sat beside each other during the film, with their hands occasionally touching on the shared armrest. Afterward, they spent time together at a private dinner away from the cameras. "The truth was simple: she was in an unhappy marriage and wanted a different life," he writes. He does not claim they had a romantic relationship, but describes their time together as "very special." He recalls growing up afraid of Kirk Douglas Douglas describes his father, Hollywood icon Kirk Douglas, as a powerful, but volatile presence. "Kirk Douglas was my father, a flawed man with a ferocious temper and a burning ambition," he writes. Douglas says his father’s behavior left him and his brother Joel frightened. He recalls Kirk saying, "I yell and scream because I care," while Douglas writes that Joel endured more of the abuse. Douglas’ cancer was misdiagnosed for nine months Douglas says doctors initially treated his persistent throat pain as an infection and prescribed multiple rounds of antibiotics. A Canadian specialist eventually discovered a subtle swelling at the back of his tongue. A biopsy revealed squamous cell carcinoma. "It’s stage IV cancer," the doctor told him, according to Douglas, who says the tumor was the size of a walnut. Douglas writes that three doctors had missed the cancer and that he had been given the wrong diagnosis for nine months. He feared surgery would require removing part of his tongue and jaw, potentially ending his acting career. His doctors publicly referred to the disease as throat cancer rather than tongue cancer because they feared reports about possible disfigurement would become sensationalized. Douglas once tried to kidnap Cameron and force him into rehab Douglas also describes the darkest years of his son Cameron’s addiction. "When he was really strung out in New York, I decided I was going to kidnap him and force him into rehab," he writes. Douglas said that Cameron was addicted to cocaine and heroin, dealt methamphetamine and carried a Glock for protection. During one incident, Cameron flashed the weapon at a drugstore and was nearly shot by police. At one point, Douglas says he arranged for two large men to help abduct Cameron and force him into rehab. "When we came back, I asked to hold the leash. Cam figured it out. He looked at me, like, ‘Dad, how could you?’ Like I had broken his heart. Again." Cameron realized what was happening and resisted, so Douglas threw the plan out of the window. Cameron later served seven years in prison after a federal drug case. Douglas writes that his son’s heroin relapse behind bars led a judge to add four and a half years to his sentence, and Cameron also spent two years in solitary confinement. articles.title: I don't think we are unserious or lack commitment: Anushka Sen
articles.summary: High-emotion storytelling and bold fashion have turned K-dramas into a global phenomenon.
articles.body: High-emotion storytelling and bold fashion have turned K-dramas into a global phenomenon. Fresh off a Korean film set, Anushka Sen talks about her experience as a Gen Z artiste abroad and her hopes for a Korean-Bollywood crossover. In a chat, the 24-year-old talks about her K-drama experience and the fresh perspective her generation brings to a film set.'I’ve had a dream to be part of a K-drama as the lead'Anushka recently made history as the first Indian actress to lead a South Korean feature film, titled Jeju Olle. Talking about the experience, she shares, "Every single day, I saw how strategic and organised they were. They’re very particular about timings and being on schedule. At the same time, it never felt like there was pressure on the actors because acting can’t be rushed. Everything was so well planned that the artists had enough time to prepare and never felt hurried."Her role in Jeju Olle was a dream come true in many ways. "When I saw my first K-drama, I absolutely fell in love with it. I fell in love with the way they show emotions and create these beautiful K-drama moments. Since then, I’ve had a dream to be part of a project where I could play the lead and have my own K-drama moment," she explains.‘It’s important to stay open to learning from others’Ask if she feels her generation is viewed as unserious, and she says, "I don’t think we are unserious or lack commitment. From being a child actor and digital creator to doing something as big as a Korean film – I’ve always been focused on growing and improving myself."She also insists that people like her have brought a different approach to film sets. "As digital creators, we’ve grown up in a fast-changing world, and I’m used to being involved in the creative process, experimenting with new ideas, connecting with different people and understanding different perspectives. But when I’m on a film set, I also keep in mind how important teamwork and respecting other’s ideas are. I think it’s about being open to learning from different perspectives while also bringing new and fresh ideas to the table."'I wish for a Korean-Bollywood crossover'For Anushka, a project like Jeju Olle couldn't come at a better time. Reflecting on the collaboration, she shares, "I think right now is a great time for a film like Jeju Olle because we’ve all seen the Korean wave, and I think it’s more than just a wave now. Everybody loves K-dramas, and personally, I’m a huge fan. At the same time, so many people across the world love Bollywood. The way we make our films and the elements we bring to our cinema are completely different from the rest of the world. I think there can be many more collaborations like this, and I would love to explore this journey further. I think Jeju Olle is just the start, and it’s a great start. India has so much to offer, and Korea has so much to offer. Together, we can create something nobody has ever thought of before and truly surprise everyone. articles.title: After Kamal Haasan, 'Ramayana' actor Kunal Kapoor criticises Elon Musk over Starlink’s India entry row, calls out ‘saviour complex of Western tech billionaires’: ‘The colonial mindset isn’t always about wanting to rule a country’
articles.summary: Actor Kunal Kapoor has criticised Elon Musk amid the ongoing debate over Starlink’s proposed entry into India, calling out what he described as the
articles.body: Actor Kunal Kapoor has criticised Elon Musk amid the ongoing debate over Starlink’s proposed entry into India, calling out what he described as the “saviour complex of Western tech billionaires”. In a strongly worded social media post, Kunal drew parallels between Musk’s past controversies in Thailand and Brazil and his recent remarks about the regulatory hurdles facing Starlink in India. His comments come after Kamal Haasan also weighed in on the controversy.Kunal Kapoor calls out Elon Musk’s ‘saviour complex’Kunal questioned the approach of powerful technology entrepreneurs who enter countries promising progress but react sharply when local institutions challenge their plans. He suggested that the response to such resistance reflects an expectation that countries should welcome these figures as problem-solvers without questioning their methods.“Watching Elon Musk this week has been a fascinating character study in the saviour complex of Western tech billionaires. They arrive in your country selling you the future. Welcome them, and you’re a country that wants progress. Make them wait, and suddenly your people are victims who need rescuing from their own institutions by the chosen one,” he wrote.The actor argued that the pattern extends beyond India, pointing to earlier disputes involving Musk in Thailand and Brazil.Kunal Kapoor recalls Elon Musk’s Thailand cave rescue controversyKunal referred to the 2018 Tham Luang cave rescue in Thailand, during which 12 young football players and their coach were trapped inside a cave complex. Musk offered a mini-submarine to assist with the rescue, but the device was not used. British diver Vernon Unsworth, who participated in the operation, questioned its practicality. Musk subsequently attacked Unsworth on social media, prompting widespread criticism.Referring to the episode, Kunal wrote, “It’s a pattern. When Thai rescuers didn’t use the mini-submarine Musk sent for the trapped boys, and diver Vernon Unsworth called the idea impractical, Musk attacked him as the ‘pedo guy.’”The actor invoked the incident to support his argument that Musk’s response to criticism follows a recurring pattern.Kunal Kapoor cites Elon Musk’s dispute with Brazil’s Supreme CourtKunal also pointed to Musk’s 2024 dispute with Brazil’s Supreme Court over orders concerning X, formerly Twitter. The platform was suspended in Brazil after it failed to comply with court orders, including requirements relating to legal representation. Musk publicly criticised the court and its judge during the dispute.“The script rarely changes. Only the country does,” Kunal wrote, drawing a comparison between the Brazil controversy and the current debate over Starlink in India.He further explained what he meant by a colonial mindset, arguing that it need not involve an explicit desire to govern another country.“The colonial mindset isn’t always about wanting to rule a country. Sometimes it’s the assumption that you arrive as its saviour, and if the country doesn’t immediately recognise you as one, something must be wrong with the country,” he added.What is the Starlink row in India?Kunal’s remarks come amid a public dispute over the delay in launching Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Musk’s SpaceX, in India. Musk has alleged that powerful business interests are obstructing the company’s entry to protect their market positions, although he has not publicly substantiated those allegations.The Indian government has rejected claims of discriminatory treatment, stating that the satellite communications approval process is fair and non-discriminatory. Authorities have said that Starlink and other licensed satellite communication operators are at broadly similar stages of the regulatory process, with security clearances and spectrum-related requirements still to be addressed.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Roma stunned as Svilar out for at least a month with stress fracture
articles.summary: There were reports Roma goalkeeper Mile Svilar had an injury, but coach Gian Piero Gasperini revealed ‘he will be out for at least a month,’ so Pierluigi Gol...
articles.body:
There were reports Roma goalkeeper Mile Svilar had an injury , but coach Gian Piero Gasperini revealed 'he will be out for at least a month,' so Pierluigi Gollini takes centre stage.

The Giallorossi have had a strong start to the season, sitting joint top of the Serie A table with Inter and Lazio, as well as earning a 1-1 Champions League draw away to Fenerbahce.

Some of that has no doubt been down to the performances of their shot-stopper, but they will be forced to do without him for some huge fixtures coming up, starting with tomorrow against Como.

Gasperini reveals true extent of Svilar injury

ISTANBUL, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 10: Mert Muldur of Fenerbahce is challenged by Mile Svilar of AS Roma during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Fenerbahce SK and AS Roma at Fenerbahce Sükrü Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi on September 10, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images)

"We have lost Svilar for a few weeks, he suffered a stress fracture in training to the fifth finger on his hand," Gasperini announced in his press conference , to the shock of the assembled media.

"The fracture will require at least a month to be fully healed. The medics are deciding whether or not to put a screw in to help stabilise it, which would allow him to return after the next break for international duty.

"It will be a heavy blow, but in a season these unexpected events do happen. We'll get Gollini ready, who will have an opportunity to get back to being important."

COMO, ITALY – MARCH 15: Mile Svilar of AS Roma is pressured by Sergi Roberto of Como 1907 during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on March 15, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Gollini is an unknown quantity for Roma now, because the 31-year-old only made one appearance for the club , in the Europa League last season for a 1-1 draw with Panathinaikos.

He hasn't featured at all in Serie A in over two years, since Genoa's 5-1 home defeat to Gasperini's Atalanta, on October 5, 2024.

ATHENS, GREECE – JANUARY 29: Pierluigi Gollini of AS Roma attempts to save a shot during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 League Phase MD8 match between Panathinaikos FC and AS Roma at Spyros Louis on January 29, 2026 in Athens, Greece. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images)

His previous clubs include Aston Villa, Atalanta, Fiorentina and Napoli.

articles.title: Sanjay Dutt recalls 1993 incident of keeping weapons in his house, says father Sunil Dutt went in shock when police put handcuffs on him: 'The mistakes were mine'
articles.summary: Sanjay Dutt was arrested in 1993 for possessing illegal firearms, including an AK-56 rifle, and was eventually sentenced to five years in prison under the
articles.body: Sanjay Dutt was arrested in 1993 for possessing illegal firearms, including an AK-56 rifle, and was eventually sentenced to five years in prison under the Arms Act. In a recent conversation with Shekhar Suman on ‘Shekhar Tonite’, the actor reflected on the decision that changed his life, admitting that he had ignored his gut feeling and failed to understand the consequences of his actions.Looking back at the incident, Sanjay said he should have trusted his instincts instead of convincing himself that keeping the weapons for a week would not lead to any trouble.“The mistakes were mine. If your heart tells you something, you should listen to it. If your mind tells you something, don’t accept it too quickly. When that incident happened and I saw what was involved, my heart told me not to do it. But my mind said, ‘Keep it for a week. What’s the harm in that?’”The actor admitted that he had not anticipated the severity of the legal consequences and emphasised that understanding the laws of the country one lives in is essential.“I had absolutely no idea what the consequences could be. I often say every person who lives in any country should know the laws of the land,” he said.During the interaction, Sanjay also revisited an emotionally difficult moment from the early days of the case, when the police handcuffed him in front of his father, veteran actor Sunil Dutt. Recalling his father's reaction, the actor said he was left stunned and broke down in tears while questioning the police about their treatment of his son.“When the police came and put handcuffs on me, my dad went into shock. With tears in his eyes, he said, ‘What are you doing with my son?’ I hugged him tight and told him, ‘Why are you letting these handcuffs bother you? Don’t be like that. It is just a procedure, please don’t be upset.’ While in reality, it was killing me from the inside. But I had to be strong for him,” he said.Although he was battling his own emotions, Sanjay said he chose to put on a brave face to comfort his father and shield him from the pain he was experiencing.“That’s how I moved throughout this trial. It went on for 24 years,” he added.Sanjay further opened up about his time behind bars, recalling how some officials expected him to struggle without the comforts and privileges associated with his celebrity status. However, he said he refused to let the circumstances break his spirit.“But nothing happened to me. Because I didn’t break. They went in shock. They mocked me. One of them came to me and said, ‘You won’t get any cigarette here. Now, what will you do?’ So my reply was, ‘Sir, I can at least get a bidi here,’” he recalled.According to the actor, his ability to adapt to the changed circumstances surprised those around him, who expected him to be more affected by life in prison.“All these changes didn’t bother me, so they got tensed that how is he so grounded and unaffected,” he added.The case against Sanjay Dutt emerged during the investigation into the serial bomb blasts that rocked Mumbai on March 12, 1993. Investigators linked the actor to the illegal possession of firearms, including an AK-56 rifle, a pistol and ammunition. He was arrested in April that year.In November 2006, a special court convicted Sanjay under the Arms Act for possessing prohibited weapons. However, he was acquitted of charges under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act (TADA) and was not convicted of participating in the bombings.In March 2013, the Supreme Court upheld his conviction but reduced his prison sentence from six years to five years. Sanjay subsequently surrendered to serve the remaining term and was lodged at Yerawada Central Jail in Pune. He was released in February 2016 after receiving remission for good conduct.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.body: Zeenat Aman may be called an icon and someone who broke stereotypes in the 70s and 80s, but off-screen, she's not seen a life that was always glamourous. She's seen many personal struggles in life, specially when it came to love. Veteran actor Raza Murad has spoken about the personal struggles of his cousin Zeenat Aman, recalling her childhood after her parents separated, her reported experience of loneliness, and the circumstances surrounding her marriage to actor Mazhar Khan. He also addressed the widely reported allegations of an alleged assault involving Sanjay Khan, which Zeenat has linked to a lasting injury to her right eye in the past.Raza reflected on Zeenat’s family background and the challenges she faced in her personal life, including her relationships and marriage.Explaining their family connection, Raza said Zeenat’s father and his mother were siblings, making them first cousins. He also revealed that Zeenat was affectionately known as Babbushah. Recalling her early years, Raza said Zeenat’s parents separated when she was young, leaving her to move between their homes. He suggested that the circumstances had a profound effect on her childhood, particularly as she was their only child.“Unfortunately, her parents separated. The effects of growing up in a broken home inevitably fall on children. She would stay with her father, and then her mother would take her away. She loved her father a lot, and he loved her dearly too,” he said in an interview with Vickey Lalwani.Raza further recalled that Zeenat attended a convent school in Panchgani, where she experienced loneliness. With both her parents eventually marrying other people, he said, she did not have the stable family environment that a child might need.“She was a single child, and her parents had separated, so a sense of loneliness naturally crept in. She did not get to experience a settled family environment. Her mother lived separately, and her father lived separately,” he added.Raza Murad recalls the alleged incident involving Zeenat Aman and Sanjay KhanRaza also addressed the long-reported controversy surrounding Zeenat’s relationship with Sanjay Khan and an alleged violent confrontation that reportedly left the actress with lasting damage to her right eye.According to Raza, Zeenat had travelled from Lonavala to Mumbai before the confrontation took place at a hotel. He described the incident as violent and said it had affected her eye.“She had rushed from Lonavala to Mumbai, and a confrontation took place there. It was a violent incident, because of which her eye was affected,” Raza said.He also reflected on relationships involving people who are already married, emphasising that those entering such relationships should consider the possible consequences. Sanjay was married to Zarine Khan at the time.“When you marry someone who is already married and has children, you have to think about it. You also need to prepare yourself mentally for the repercussions,” he said.However, Raza made it clear that he did not consider violence against women acceptable under any circumstances.“Whatever happened was wrong. You have no right to raise your hand against a woman,” he said.Zeenat and Sanjay reportedly married in 1978, while he was still married to Zarine. Sanjay and Zeenat’s marriage was short-lived. Sanjay’s daughter Farah has previously confirmed that her father married Zeenat while he was still married to her mother.Over the years, reports have linked the alleged assault to a confrontation at a Mumbai hotel, where Zeenat reportedly sustained serious injuries to her right eye.Zeenat Aman on dealing with the alleged abuseZeenat has spoken publicly about experiencing physical abuse, although she has not always identified the person involved in her remarks. During a 1999 appearance on Simi Garewal’s show, ‘Rendezvous with Simi Garewal’, she described how she coped with the painful memories.“For many years, in my mind, it’s been obliterated because I think that’s what the human mind does. When there is something distinctly unpleasant, you just close your mind to it and pretend that it never happened and you promise yourself that it will never happen again. And that’s how you cope,” she said.The actress has also discussed the long-term effects of her eye injury. In a subsequent Instagram post, she explained that the injury had caused her eyelid to droop and affected her vision.Sanjay Khan denies allegations of assaultSanjay Khan, however, has denied the allegations surrounding the alleged assault and disputed claims that he was responsible for Zeenat’s eye condition.In a conversation with Hrishikesh Kannan while discussing his autobiography, ‘The Best Mistakes of My Life’, Sanjay described the accounts circulating about the incident as one-sided and said he had not been given an opportunity to present his version.“I was so pained and horrified with the one-sidedness of the entire story because nobody even asked me what happened. This was a well planned PR attack against me which came like a blitzkrieg,” he said.He also denied slapping Zeenat and attributed her eye condition to heredity.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: ‘Breaking Bad’ star Aaron Paul is ready to part with his historic Los Angeles home, which he bought in 2019. The actor originally listed the home for USD 10 million in July 2025. Now, according to the listing on Serhant, the home has officially sold for USD 7.5 million.Aaron Paul sells off his LA home after 7 years of ownershipLocated at 2666 Aberdeen Avenue, Los Angeles, CA 90027, Aaron Paul bought his historic Los Angeles home in 2019. Almost seven years later, the actor has officially sold the property. The listing shared online that the property sold for USD 7.49 million.The property is one of the few homes constructed in the hills above LA’s Los Feliz neighborhood. Known as the Seyler House, it is one of the first four-bedroom, three-and-a-half-bathroom properties, now sitting on 1.5 acres just underneath the Griffith Park area. While talking to PEOPLE when the property was first put up for sale, the actor shared it will always hold a special place in his heart. At the time he shared that the house “has been a safe haven for my family, and we feel so lucky to have experienced so much life here over the years." We will forever hold this home and its history close to our hearts.”Why Aaron Paul sold off his property in LAThe actor had opened up about how he had been planning on shifting his family to Paris soon and that they did not wish to live in Los Angeles anymore. While talking to Travel + Leisure in an old interview, the actor had opened up about the Paris move, sharing that after the Southern California wildfires in January last year, Paul and his wife Lauren had moved with their daughter Story, 8, and son Ryden, 4, to Europe.He shared at the time, “We have always dreamt of doing a year abroad. Specifically in Paris. Love the food, the history, and the people. Every time I came to Paris, I never wanted to leave. We wanted our kids to learn another language and be surrounded by another culture. It was very important to us.”More about Aaron Paul’s LA mansionThe property was originally built in 1922 and was built by famed architect Stiles O.
